Scrub the outside of all melons thoroughly before cutting to remove any soil bacteria. Remove the rinds and all seeds.
Safety First: Avoid using a melon baller for children under 5. The round spheres are a significant choking risk as they are firm and slippery.
6-9 Months: Slice the melons into long, flat rectangular fingers (about the size of two adult fingers). This allows babies to grip the fruit in their palm and gum the end.
9-12 Months: Once the pincer grip develops, cut the fruit into flat, bite-sized pieces or small sticks roughly the size of a thumb.
1-5 Years: Serve as small, thin chunks or wedges. Ensure pieces are not so large that a child might attempt to swallow them whole.
Serving Guide 6-9 Months (Early Weaning): Preparation - mashed or long, flat rectangular fingers (size of two adult fingers); Portion - 2-3 thin fingers for self-feeding.
Serving Guide 9-12 Months (Pincer Grasp): Preparation - small, flat bite-sized chunks or thin thumb-sized sticks; Portion - a small handful of pieces.
Serving Guide 1-5 Years (Pre-school): Preparation - mixed medley of thin chunks or small wedges; Portion - 1 small bowl (approx. 40g-50g).

Under 1s Olds: 1 oatcake, 20g fruit, 20g veg
3-4 Year Olds: 1.5-2 oatcakes, 40g fruit, 40g veg

ingredients.name: Whole meal pittas (10-12, cut in half to make)

method: Make the Sauce: Simmer the lentils, mushrooms, grated onion, tomatoes, water, and oregano in a pan for 15-20 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and the sauce is thick. Blend until smooth so it spreads easily and hides the lentils from picky eaters.
Assemble: Lay the pitta halves on a baking tray. Spread a generous tablespoon of the lentil-tomato sauce over each.
Cheese: Sprinkle a small amount of grated cheese on top (keep it light to manage saturated fat/salt levels).
Bake: Grill or bake at 180°C for 5-8 minutes until the cheese is melted and the pitta is warm but still soft (do not overcook, as hard pitta is a choking risk for infants).
Lightly toast the Wholemeal bagel halves.
Cut each bagel half into 4 smaller segments (triangles) or "soldiers" to make them safer and easier for small hands to hold.
Serve with the sliced banana
Portions - 1-2 years: 1/2 Wholemeal Bagel with mashed or banana slices
Portions - 2-3 years: 1/2 Wholemeal Bagel with banana slices
Portions - 3-5 years: 1 Wholemeal Bagel with banana slice

ingredients.name: Organic cherry tomatoes: must be quartered lengthways (side salad)

method: Sauté: Soften the onions, grated carrots, grated courgettes in a splash of water for 10-12 minutes.
Brown: Add the beef mince to the pan. Cook until browned, breaking up any large lumps. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Simmer: Pour in the tinned tomatoes and herbs. Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes. The grated carrots will melt into the sauce, naturally thickening and sweetening it.
Pasta: Cook the wholewheat spaghetti in boiling water for 10-12 minutes until tender. Drain, then toss with the sauce.
Serve with side salad

ingredients.name: Organic cherry tomatoes: must be quartered lengthways (side salad)

method: Sauté: Soften the onions, grated carrots, grated courgette in a splash of water for 10-12 minutes.
Brown: Add the Lentils to the pan. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Simmer: Pour in the tinned tomatoes and herbs. Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes. The grated carrots will melt into the sauce, naturally thickening and sweetening it.
Pasta: Cook the wholewheat spaghetti in boiling water for 10-12 minutes until tender. Drain, then toss with the sauce.
Serve with side salad
Prep the Fruit: Place the frozen fruit in a saucepan with 100ml of the water. Simmer on low heat for 5-8 minutes until the fruit breaks down into a thick, purple/red "jam."
Mix: In a large bowl, combine the oats and cinnamon.

Combine: Pour the hot fruit mixture over the oats. Add the remaining 100ml-150ml of boiling water gradually, stirring until the oats are fully soaked and sticky. (If using mashed bananas, stir them in now.)
Press: Line a large baking tray with greaseproof paper. Spread the mixture out and press it down firmly with the back of a spoon until it is about 2cm thick.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15 minutes until the edges are slightly golden but the middle is still soft.
Cool & Cut: Let them cool completely in the tin before slicing into 20 squares or fingers. This helps them "set" so they don't crumble.
Cut into fingers (Soft for babies)
1-2 Year Olds: Serve 2-3 fingers (approx. 1/4 to 1/2 pitta). 40g fruit/veg
3-4 Year Olds: Serve 4 fingers (a full 1/2 pitta). 80g fruit/veg

ingredients.name: Organic cherry tomatoes (must be quartered lengthways)
Mild cheddar (grated) (use Violife cheese for Dairy/free)
Greek style yoghurt (use oatly yoghurt for Dairy/free) (potato salad)

method: Sauté: Soften the onion and spinach in a pan until the spinach has wilted. Drain all excess liquid thoroughly.
Whisk: Beat the eggs and milk together with the herbs.
Assemble: Grease two large baking tins. Spread the spinach/onion mix across the bottom. Pour over the egg mixture.
Top: Scatter the quartered cherry tomatoes and grated cheese on top.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 20-25 minutes until set and golden. Let cool for 15 minutes before slicing into 20 squares.
Potato salad - Wash the potatoes (leave skins on for fibre) and boil in water for 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Potato salad - Chop: Once cooled, cut into bite-sized cubes (approx. 1cm).
Potato salad - Mix: Gently fold the yoghurt, lemon juice, and herbs into the potatoes until coated. (text cut off at bottom of source card)

ingredients.name: Organic cherry tomatoes (must be quartered lengthways)

method: Boil Potatoes: Boil the potatoes in water for 15-20 minutes until very tender (fork-soft). Drain and let cool slightly.
Make Dressing: In a large bowl, whisk the yoghurt, lemon juice, olive oil, and herbs until smooth.
Combine: Add the warm potatoes and the rinsed kidney beans to the dressing. Toss gently so the potatoes are well coated.
Fold in Veg: Stir in the shredded spinach (the warmth from the potatoes will wilt it slightly). Finally, fold in the quartered cherry tomatoes.
Cool: Let the salad sit for 10 minutes before serving to allow the flavours to meld

ingredients.name: Organic milk (use Oatly milk for Dairy/free)

method: Prepare the Pears: Peel and core the pears. Steam or boil them in a small amount of water for 5-8 minutes until very soft. Mash them thoroughly.
Cook the Oats: In a large pot, combine the oats, milk, water, and cinnamon.
Simmer: Bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until creamy and the oats are soft.
Combine: Stir the mashed pear directly into the porridge. If it's too thick, add a splash more milk or water.
Cool: Let the porridge sit for a few minutes before serving. It should be warm, not hot, for young children.

ingredients.name: Ground coriander (mild and earthy - no chilli)
Organic carrots (peeled and cut into sticks/batons) (10-12) (side)

method: Soften the onions and grated carrots in a splash of olive oil for 8-10 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, sweet potato, cauliflower, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20-25 minutes until the lentils have "melted" and the vegetables are very soft.
Stir in the coconut milk for the last 5 minutes. If it's too thick, add a splash more water to reach a "spoonable" consistency.
Sides - Boil the brown rice in unsalted water for 25-30 minutes until tender. Note: For infants under 12 months, overcook the rice slightly so it is very soft and easy to gum.
Sides - Steam or boil the carrot sticks for 8-10 minutes until "fork-tender" (they must be soft enough to squash between a thumb and finger).
Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a large rectangular baking tin.
Sift the flour and sweet cinnamon into a large bowl.
Whisk the Oatly and the 50ml oil together.
Pour the wet mix into the flour. Fold in the finely grated carrots and the raisins (including all the soaking water).
Pour into the tin. Bake for 35-45 minutes. Since there is no egg or banana, it needs the full time to set.
Cool: Let it cool completely before slicing into 20 squares.

ingredients.name: Water (add gradually until you have a soft dough)

method: Preheat to 200°C (180°C fan). Line one large baking tray.
Whisk the flour, bicarb, baking powder, garlic, and chives in a bowl.
Blend the beetroot with the olive oil.
Make a well in the flour. Add the beetroot and most of the water. Stir until it forms a soft, slightly sticky dough (add the rest of the water only if it's too crumbly).
On a floured surface, pat the dough into one large rectangle about 2cm thick.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. It should feel firm and sound hollow when you tap the bottom.
Portion serves 20: Beetroot Bread - 40 fingers total (2 per child); 40g Fruit; 40g Veg Sticks

ingredients.name: Organic Olive oil (to sauté garlic and veg)

method: Briefly heat the olive oil in a pan. Add the minced garlic, diced pepper, and grated courgette. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until soft. This "mellows" the garlic and ensures the veg is tender for younger children.
In a bowl, combine the sautéed veg with the drained tuna, sweetcorn, and ground black pepper. Stir well so the pepper is evenly distributed.
Lay out the tortillas. Sprinkle cheese on one half, top with the tuna-garlic-veg mix, and add another sprinkle of cheese.
Fold in half. bake on a tray at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the garlic aroma is released.
Let them rest for a minute so the cheese sets, then slice into fingers or triangles.
Portions - 6-12 Months: 1-2 long fingers + 2-3 soft sticks (peeled).
Portions - 1-2 Years: 2 triangles + 3-4 batons.
Portions - 3-5 Years: 2-3 triangles + 4-5 slices.

ingredients.name: Organic cannellini beans rinsed and lightly mashed
Organic Olive oil (to sauté the garlic and veg)

method: Briefly heat the olive oil in a pan. Add the minced garlic, diced pepper, and grated courgette. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until soft. This "mellows" the garlic and ensures the veg is tender for younger children.
In a bowl, combine the sautéed veg with the slightly mashed beans, sweetcorn, and ground black pepper. Stir well so the pepper is evenly distributed.
Lay out the tortillas. Sprinkle cheese on one half, top with the tuna-garlic-veg mix, and add another sprinkle of cheese.
Fold in half. bake on a tray at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the garlic aroma is released.
Let them rest for a minute so the cheese sets, then slice into fingers or triangles.
Portions - 6-12 Months: 1-2 long fingers + 40g soft veg
Portions - 1-2 Years: 2 triangles + 80g veg
Portions - 3-5 Years: 2-3 triangles + 80g veg

Portions - 2-3 yrs: 1/2-1 Weetabix, 120-150ml milk, 2-3 tbsp banana

Roll into small, sausage-shaped "fingers" (approx. 40 total).

ingredients.name: Organic Greek style Yoghurt (Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for Vegan/Dairy free)

method: Core the apples. Peel them for children under 1 to remove the choking risk. Slice each apple into 8 even wedges.
Place wedges in a baking dish. Pour over the 4 tbsp water and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Cover the dish tightly with foil to trap the steam.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15-20 minutes until "fork-tender" (they should squash easily between your fingers).
Let them cool. Serve the soft wedges with a dollop of plain yoghurt for dipping.
Cut into fingers (Soft for babies)
1-2 Year Olds: Serve 1.5 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg
3-4 Year Olds: Serve 2 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg
Prep Mango: Ensure the 125g of mango is thawed. Mash it with a fork (or puree for under 1s) to a smooth consistency.
Prepare Chickpeas: Place the drained chickpeas in a large bowl. For Under 1s: mash into a smooth, thick paste (no whole beans). For Over 1s: mash roughly so some texture remains.
Mix Filling: Stir in the mashed mango, dairy-free yoghurt, mild curry powder, turmeric, black pepper, grated carrot, and diced onion.
Assemble: Spread the filling generously onto the Wholemeal bread.
Slice for Ages: 6-12 Months - remove crusts and cut into thin, soft fingers. 1-5 Years - cut into triangles or squares.
Serve: Plate with 80g of crudités (e.g., 40g cucumber and 40g pepper sticks).
Mash: In a large bowl, mash the bananas into a liquid-like paste.
Mix: Whisk in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and dairy-free milk until you have a thick, smooth batter.
Cook: Heat a drop of oil in a non-stick pan. Pour small circles (8cm wide).
Flip: Cook until bubbles form on top (approx. 2 mins), flip, and cook for 1 min more.
Yield: Aim for 40-60 small pancakes (2-3 per child).
Portions - 6-12 Months (Early Weaning): 1-2 small pancakes cut into thin, soft "fingers"; Fruit (80g total): very soft-steamed fruit pieces.
Portions - 1-2 Years (Toddlers): 2 small pancakes (halved for easier handling); Fruit (80g total)
Portions - 3-5 Years (Pre-school): 2-3 small pancakes; Fruit (80g total)
Rice: Boil the rice in a large pan of unsalted water until soft and fluffy. Drain and set aside.
Side Veg: Steam or boil the cauliflower florets for 6-8 minutes until "fork-tender" (soft enough to squish easily). Set aside.
Aromatic Base: In a large wide pan, heat a splash of oil. Gently sauté the grated ginger and crushed garlic for 1 minute (do not brown).
Spice it up: Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander for 30 seconds to release the aroma.
Creamy Sauce: Pour in the 2 tins of coconut milk and add the grated lime zest. Bring to a very gentle simmer.
Add Veg: Stir the diced courgettes, peas, and sweetcorn into the sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Cook Salmon: Gently add the 1kg salmon chunks to the simmering sauce. Cook for 5-8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily. Critical: Check every piece for tiny pin-bones before serving.
The Finish: Stir in the lime juice right at the end to keep the flavours fresh and bright.

ingredients.name: Cauliflower (approx. 2 medium heads, cut into small florets)

method: Rice: Boil the rice in unsalted water until soft and fluffy.
Side Veg: Steam or boil the cauliflower for 6-8 minutes until very soft (fork-tender).
Aromatic Base: Gently sauté the grated ginger and crushed garlic in a splash of oil for 1 minute.
Spice: Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander for 30 seconds.
Creamy Sauce: Pour in the coconut milk and add the lime zest. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add Veg & Beans: Stir in the diced courgettes, peas, sweetcorn, and the drained white beans.
Simmer: Cook gently for 10-12 minutes so the beans soften further and the courgettes are tender.
Finish: Stir in the lime juice right before serving.

method: Defrost raspberries as per manufacturer's instructions.
Mash the fruit a little and mash, add to yoghurt and stir.
Cover with cling film and refrigerate at 8°C or below until serving.

ingredients.name: Large wholemeal wraps (3-4, cut into 8 triangles each = 24-32 pieces)
Fruit (chose from plums, peaches, grapes quartered)

method: 6-12 Months: 1 triangle (20g fruit, 20g veg (Soft))
1-2 Years: 1.5 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg)
3-5 Years: 2 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg)
Cook the chicken in boiling water until tender. Shred it into very fine pieces while warm, then let it cool.
Boil the rice noodles in unsalted water until soft. Drain and immediately rinse in cold water to stop them sticking.
Lightly steam the grated carrots and diced peppers for 5-8 minutes until soft enough to squash.
Peel the cucumbers and scoop out the watery seeds. Cut the remaining flesh into thin matchsticks or a fine dice.
Whisk the olive oil, water, 5-spice, garlic, and ginger until combined.
In a large mixing bowl, toss the cold noodles, shredded chicken, steamed carrots/peppers, and the prepared cucumber together.
Pour the 5-spice dressing over the mixture and toss thoroughly until every strand is coated.

Prep Chickpeas: Rinse the chickpeas, boil in a pan with 1tsp of baking powder - this helps break down the skin. For Under 1s: mash them into a rough paste or pulse in a blender so there are no whole round beans (choking risk). For 1-5 Years: leave them whole or lightly "smash" them with a fork so they mix better with the noodles.
Cook Noodles: Boil rice noodles in unsalted water until soft. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Steam (For Under 1s): Lightly steam the grated carrots and diced peppers for 5-8 minutes until soft.
Make Dressing: Whisk the olive oil, water, 5-spice, garlic, and ginger.
Combine: In a large bowl, toss the cold noodles, chickpeas, and all 1.6kg of vegetables.
Dress: Pour the dressing over and mix thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Organic milk (use Oatly milk for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Prepare the apples: peel and core them. Steam or boil in a small amount of water for 5-8 minutes until very soft. Mash thoroughly.
Cook the oats: in a large pot, combine the oats, milk, water, and cinnamon.
Simmer: bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until creamy and the oats are soft.
Combine: stir the mashed apple directly into the porridge. If it's too thick, add a splash more milk or water.
Cool: let the porridge sit for a few minutes before serving. It should be warm, not hot, for young children.
In a large pan, brown the turkey mince. Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the grated carrots and courgettes. Cook gently for 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Pour in the 3 tins of tomatoes, beans, and herbs. Simmer on low for 25-30 minutes.
Boil the brown rice in a separate pan for 25-30 minutes until tender.
While the chilli is simmering, steam or boil your sweetcorn 4-5 minutes.
Place a portion of brown rice on the plate, ladle the turkey chilli over the top, and serve the side of sweetcorn.
In a large pan, add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the grated carrots, courgettes, sweetcorn. Cook gently for 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Pour in the 3 tins of tomatoes, beans, and herbs. Simmer on low for 25-30 minutes.
Boil the brown rice in a separate pan for 25-30 minutes until tender.
While the chilli is simmering, steam or boil your sweetcorn 4-5 minutes.
Place a portion of brown rice on the plate, ladle the turkey chilli over the top, and serve the side of peas.

ingredients.name: Organic Pears (Make sure they are ripe and soft for toddlers)
Organic Bananas (Add at the very last minute to prevent browning)

method: Wash all fruit thoroughly. Peel the melon and remove any seeds.
Dice the melon, apples, and pears into small, bite-sized chunks (approx. 1cm). Keeping the skin on the apples and pears adds extra fibre, which is great for digestion.
Peel the oranges/satsumas. Remove as much white pith as possible. Cut each segment into 2 or 3 smaller pieces so they are easy for toddlers to chew.
Toss the diced melon, apple, pear, and orange pieces together in a large bowl. If not serving immediately, stir in a little orange juice to keep the fruit fresh.
Just before serving, peel and slice the bananas into coins and fold them in gently.
Divide into 20 small bowls.

ingredients.name: Large wholemeal wraps (cut into 8 triangles each = 24-32 pieces)

method: Cut into fingers/triangles.
6-12 Months: 1 triangle (20g fruit - 20g veg (Soft))
1-2 Years: 1.5 triangles (40g fruit - 40g veg)
3-5 Years: 2 triangles (40g fruit - 40g veg)
Boil the Wholemeal pasta until tender (approx. 10-12 mins). Drain and rinse under cold water immediately to stop the cooking and cool it down.
While the pasta cools, finely dice your peppers and tomatoes. Thaw your peas by running them under warm water, then cold.
In a small bowl, mash one of the avocados with the lime juice and olive oil until smooth. This acts as your "sauce."
In a large mixing bowl, toss the cold pasta with the kidney beans, diced peppers, tomatoes, and peas.
Pour the mashed avocado dressing over the pasta and stir well until everything is creamy and coated.
Dice the second avocado into small cubes and gently fold it in so there are some chunky bits for the children to find.
Serve cold.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Add the Oatly and whisk until well combined and frothy.
Add the oil to a large non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture. Let it sit for 20 seconds, then gently stir with a spatula. Keep moving slowly until they are soft and creamy. Do not overcook, as they will become rubbery.
While the eggs are cooking, toast the wholewheat bread.
Spread the eggs evenly over the toast. For toddlers, it is best to cut the toast into "soldiers" (strips) to make it easier for them to pick up.
Serve with 1 selection of fruit. Make sure these are soft fingers for babies so part boil.
Heat a splash of oil in a large pot. Add the onions, garlic, and diced peppers. Cook gently for 8-10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the courgettes and all the dry spices (coriander, paprika, turmeric). Cook for 2 minutes until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the 3 tins of chopped tomatoes and the chopped apricots. Add the rinsed chickpeas. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Place the dry couscous in a large heatproof bowl. Pour over 500ml of boiling water. Cover the bowl with a lid or cling film and leave for 5-8 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
Use a fork to fluff up the couscous so there are no lumps.
Ladle the Moroccan chickpea stew over the fluffy couscous. Serve with a side of steamed green beans.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-Style Yoghurt (Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy free)
Satsumas/clementines (easy to peel usually seedless) or Oranges

method: Peel the oranges or satsumas. Remove as much of the white stringy pith as possible.
Cut each segment into 2 or 3 bite-sized pieces. For younger toddlers, you can "supreme" the oranges (removing the skin/membrane) so they are extra soft, but small chopped segments are usually fine.
Place a generous dollop of yoghurt into 20 small bowls or ramekins.
Divide the orange pieces evenly across the bowls, sitting them on top of the yoghurt.
Sprinkle with a tiny bit of sweet cinnamon if you like. Serve chilled.
Cut into fingers.
Under 1s Olds: 1 oatcake 20g fruit - 20g veg
3-4 Year Olds: 1.5-2 oatcakes 40g fruit - 40g veg

ingredients.name: Organic Greek style Yoghurt (Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for dairy free)

method: Drain the tuna thoroughly and flake it in a bowl. Mix in the finely diced peppers and sweetcorn.
Add the Greek style yoghurt and a pinch of black pepper. Stir until creamy. Tip: Adding the peppers and corn into the mix ensures every bite has Vitamin C to boost iron absorption.
Spread the mixture onto half of the Wholemeal bread slices. Top with the remaining slices and remove the crusts if serving younger babies.
Cut into small triangles or "soldiers" (fingers) which are easier for toddlers to hold.
Peel the carrots. Cut the carrots and cucumber into thin, finger-length sticks (batons). Safety Tip: Quarter the cucumber lengthways first so the sticks aren't too wide.
Place 2 triangles on each plate with a few carrot and cucumber sticks on the side.
Pat the tofu dry with a paper towel. Use a fork to mash the tofu in a large bowl until it looks like "flaked" tuna (small, irregular crumbles).
Stir in the sweetcorn and the finely diced red peppers.
Tip: The peppers and lemon juice provide the Vitamin C needed to help children absorb the plant-based iron from the tofu.
Fold in the Oatly Greek Style and the herbs/pepper. Stir until you have a thick, spreadable consistency.
Spread the mixture onto the Wholemeal bread. Top with another slice and cut into small, toddler-friendly triangles or "soldiers."
Peel the carrots and cut both the carrots and cucumber into finger-length sticks (batons).
Safety: Quarter the cucumber lengthways before slicing so the sticks are not too thick for small mouths.
Place 2 triangles on each plate with a few crudites on the side.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-style Yoghurt (use Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy free)

method: Place the dry oats and sweet cinnamon in a large pan over a medium heat. Stir for 2-3 minutes until they smell slightly toasty.
Turn off the heat. Pour the 150ml of boiling water over the toasted oats and stir well.
Cover the pan and let the oats sit for 10 minutes. They will soak up the water and become soft and "chewy" rather than hard and crunchy, making them safe for small children.
While the oats rest, peel the kiwis and dice them into small, 1cm cubes.
Place a generous dollop of Greek yoghurt into 20 small bowls.
Top each bowl with a spoonful of the softened cinnamon oats and the diced kiwi.
Stir slightly before giving to the children so the yoghurt coats the oats.
Part-boil the sliced potatoes in a large pot for 5-8 minutes until they are slightly soft but not falling apart. Drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, saute the onions and leeks in a tiny bit of oil until soft and sweet (approx. 8 minutes).
Pour the Oatly Whole and the herbs into the pan with the onions/leeks. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the corn flour mix and keep stirring until the sauce thickens.

In a large baking dish, layer half of the par-boiled potatoes. Top with the raw salmon chunks, then pour over half of the creamy sauce. Layer the remaining potatoes on top and pour over the rest of the sauce.
Place in a preheated oven at 180C (160C fan) for 25-30 minutes until the salmon is cooked through and the top is golden.
Boil or steam the frozen peas for 3 minutes. Serve the gratin with the peas on the side.
Boil the sliced potatoes in a large pot for 6-8 minutes until they are slightly tender but still hold their shape. Drain and set aside.
In a large pan, saute the onions and leeks in a splash of oil until they are very soft and sweet (approx. 10 minutes).
Pour the Oatly Whole and the herbs into the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the corn flour mix and keep stirring until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
In a large ovenproof dish, layer half of the par-boiled potatoes and all of the rinsed butterbeans. Pour over half the sauce. Top with the remaining potatoes and the rest of the sauce.
Place in a preheated oven at 180C (160C fan) for 25-30 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the top is golden.
Steam the frozen peas for 3 minutes. Serve a square of the gratin with a side of peas.
Preheat oven to 180C (160C fan). Line a large rectangular baking tin with parchment paper (since there's no oil, it may stick to a plain greased tin).
Sift the flour, mixed spice, and bicarb into a large bowl.
Mix your soaked raisins (and their liquid) with the extra Oatly.
Pour the wet mix into the dry. Add the frozen fruit last. Stir gently until just combined. Do not over-mix, or the gluten will make the oil-free sponge gummy.
Pour into the tin. Bake for 35-45 minutes. Because it's oil-free, it needs to be fully set - check with a skewer.
Let it cool completely in the tin. Oil-free bakes need time to "set" their structure before slicing into 20 squares.
Cut into fingers.
1-2 Year Olds: Serve 1.5 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg
3-4 Year Olds: Serve 2 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg

ingredients.name: fresh mint or 1 tsp dried mint

method: Toss the chicken cubes in the olive oil, lemon juice, and oregano. Let it sit for 10 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Saute the chicken in a large non-stick pan over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until cooked through and slightly golden. Ensure the pieces are small enough for toddlers to chew safely.
While the chicken cooks, stir the chopped mint and grated cucumber into the oatly yoghurt.
Lightly toast the Wholemeal pittas and cut them into strips (soldiers) or small pockets.
Place the chicken alongside the pitta fingers and a dollop of the mint yoghurt dip.
Add the pepper and carrot sticks on the side (Part boil for babies).

ingredients.name: fresh mint or 1 tsp dried mint

method: Toss the drained cannellini beans and diced peppers in the olive oil, garlic, and oregano. Spread on a large tray and roast at 200C (180C fan) for 15-20 minutes until the peppers are soft.
While the chickpeas roast, grate half the cucumber. Put it in a clean tea towel and squeeze out all the water.
In a bowl, stir the squeezed cucumber, 500g Oatly Oatgurt, chopped mint, and 1 tbsp fresh lemon. Set aside in the fridge to stay cool.
Once the chickpeas are out of the oven, lightly squash them with a fork. This stops them from rolling out of the pitta and removes the "round food" choking hazard for toddlers.
Briefly warm the pittas in the oven or toaster. Open the pockets and put 1 heaped teaspoon of the Mint Dip inside first (this acts as a "glue"), then fill with the roasted chickpea and pepper mix.
Place the stuffed pitta half on a plate with the remaining cucumber/carrot sticks on the side for extra crunch. (Part boil for babies).

ingredients.name: cream cheese (Violife Creamy Original for vegan/dairy free)

method: Peel, core, and slice the pears into soft, thin segments. If they are very firm, steam them for 2 minutes so they are easy for toddlers to chew.
Lightly toast the Wholemeal bagel halves.
Spread a generous layer of cream cheese onto each warm bagel half. (Violife Creamy for vegan/dairy free)
Cut each bagel half into 4 smaller segments (triangles) or "soldiers" to make them safer and easier for small hands to hold.
Serve with the sliced pears.
Portions - 1-2 years: 1/2 Wholemeal Bagel with 1 heaped tsp (15g) Cream Cheese and 2-3 soft Pear slices.
Portions - 2-3 years: 1/2 Wholemeal Bagel with 2 tsp (20g) Cream Cheese and 3-4 soft Pear slices.
Portions - 3-5 years: 1 Wholemeal Bagel with 1 tbsp (30g) Cream Cheese and 4-5 soft Pear slices.
Boil the Wholemeal spaghetti in a large pot until tender (approx. 10-12 mins). Drain and set aside. Tip: Use clean kitchen scissors to snip the spaghetti into smaller strands for younger toddlers.
Heat a splash of oil in a large pan. Cook the chicken cubes with the garlic and ginger until the chicken is white all the way through.
Stir in the diced peppers and grated carrots. Cook for 5-8 minutes until soft.
Pour in the 3 tins of tomatoes and the tomato puree. Stir well.
Add the frozen pineapple chunks. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes. The pineapple will release its sweetness and the sauce will thicken.
While the sauce simmers, steam or boil the broccoli florets for 4-5 minutes until tender but still bright green.
Toss the cooked spaghetti into the sweet and sour sauce. Stir thoroughly so every strand is coated.
Divide the spaghetti and chicken mix into 20 bowls and serve the steamed broccoli on the side.
Boil the Wholemeal spaghetti in a large pot until tender (approx. 10-12 mins). Drain and set aside. Tip: Use clean kitchen scissors to snip the spaghetti into smaller strands for younger toddlers.
Pat the tofu cubes dry. Heat a splash of oil in a large pan and lightly saute the tofu for 5 minutes until the edges are firm. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add the diced peppers and grated carrots. Cook for 5-8 minutes until soft.
Pour in the 3 tins of tomatoes and the tomato puree. Stir well.
Stir in the frozen pineapple chunks and the sauteed tofu. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the pineapple is soft and the sauce is thick and sweet.
While the sauce simmers, steam or boil the broccoli florets for 4-5 minutes until tender but still bright green.
Toss the cooked spaghetti into the sweet and sour sauce. Stir thoroughly so every strand is coated (this makes it easier for toddlers to handle).
Divide the spaghetti and tofu mix into 20 bowls and serve the broccoli on the side.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-Style Yoghurt (use Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy free - card notes this substitute 'Contains gluten')

method: Defrost Mango fruits as per manufacturer's instructions.
Mash the fruit a little and mash, add to yoghurt and stir.
Cover with cling film and refrigerate at 8C or below until serving.
Cut into fingers.
1-2 Year Olds: Serve 2-3 fingers (approx. 1/4 to 1/2 pitta). 40g fruit/veg
3-4 Year Olds: Serve 4 fingers (a full 1/2 pitta). 80g fruit/veg
Boil the rice until tender, drain, and let it cool completely.
Heat the oil and quickly fry the garlic and ginger.
Add the diced carrots and peppers first (they take longer), then toss in the frozen peas and corn. Cook until the carrots are soft enough for toddlers.
Push the veg to the side. Pour in all 10-12 beaten eggs. Scramble them until they are just set, then fold them into the vegetables.
Mix in the cooled rice. Stir thoroughly until steaming hot throughout to meet food safety standards.
Rinse canned chickpeas thoroughly. For younger children, you can slightly mash them with a fork to reduce the risk of choking and make them easier to eat.
Heat the oil and saute the garlic, ginger, carrots, and peppers until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the chickpeas, frozen peas, and sweetcorn. Cook for 3-5 minutes until heated through.
Add the pre-cooked, cooled rice. Toss everything together until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: Organic milk or fortified plant milk (use fortified plant milk for vegan/dairy free)

method: Peel the oranges, remove as much of the white stringy pith.
Safety cut each segment into 2-3 pieces; for younger babies you can supreme the orange (cutting the membrane out of the orange so it's soft).
Serve 1/2-1 biscuit per child depending on age.
Add milk to soften.
1-2 yrs: 1/2 Weetabix, 60-120ml milk, 1-2 segments cut into small pieces.
2-3 yrs: 1/2-1 Weetabix, 120-150ml milk, 2-3 segments cut into small pieces.
3-5 yrs: 1 Weetabix, 150ml milk, 3-4 cut into small pieces.
Cook onions, leeks, mushrooms, and carrots in a large pot with a splash of water for 15 mins until very soft and sweet.
Add beef and cook until browned. Stir in tomato puree and thyme.
Add 1.2L water. Simmer for 40 mins until thick. If it's too thin, mash some of the cooked carrots into the sauce to thicken it.
Boil potatoes in plain water. Drain, but keep 100ml of the starchy potato water. Mash the potatoes. Spread the meat in a tray, top with mash, and bake at 190C until golden.
Steam shredded spring greens & kale for 4 mins. Serve plain to let the natural sweetness of the greens shine.

Heat 1 tbsp of vegetable oil in a large pot. Add the onions, leeks, mushrooms, and carrots. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes with a splash of water until they are very soft. This creates the natural "sweetness" since you aren't using sugar or stock.
Stir in the rinsed red lentils, tomato puree, and dried thyme.
Pour in the 1.8L of water. Bring to a boil, then turn down to a simmer. Cover and cook for about 20-25 minutes.
Tip: The lentils should be completely soft and have absorbed most of the water to create a thick "gravy." If it looks too dry, add a splash more water.
Boil the potatoes in plain water until tender. Drain, keeping a small cup of the starchy water.
Pour the lentil mixture into your baking trays. Spread the potato mash over the top. Bake at 190C for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden.
Steam the shredded greens & kale for 4 minutes and serve immediately alongside the pie.
Preheat oven to 180C (160C fan). Line a muffin tin with 20 mini-muffin cases or grease a tin well.
Sift the Wholemeal flour, bicarb, and baking powder into a bowl (tip any bran left in the sieve back into the bowl).
In a separate bowl, whisk the mashed bananas and Oatly together until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir gently until just combined - do not over-mix, Wholemeal flour or the muffins will be heavy.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Spoon into cases. Bake for 15-20 minutes (for mini muffins) or 20-25 minutes (for larger ones) until they spring back when touched.
Let them cool completely. Wholemeal, oil-free bakes can be a bit sticky when hot, so they are best served once cooled.
Grate the carrots and courgettes. Wrap them in a clean tea towel and squeeze out all the water. If you skip this, the bread will be soggy.
Put the flour and herbs into a large bowl.
Stir in the squeezed vegetables and the vegetable oil.
Gradually pour in the Oatly, stirring with a wooden spoon until it forms a soft, thick dough (it should not be runny like cake batter, but firm like bread dough).
Press the dough into a lined baking tray (about 2cm thick). Score the top into "fingers" with a knife before baking.
Bake at 200C (180C fan) for 25-30 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Let it cool slightly, then cut along your score lines into "Micky Me-Size" fingers.
Cut into fingers.
1-2 Year Olds: Serve 2-3 fingers. 40g fruit/veg
3-4 Year Olds: Serve 4 fingers. 80g fruit/veg

ingredients.name: Organic plain Greek style yoghurt (use Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy free)

method: Saute the onions, ginger, and garlic in oil for 10 mins until soft.
Add the turmeric, coriander, and cumin. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, sweet potato, tomatoes, spinach and water.
Simmer for 25-30 mins until the lentils and sweet potatoes are "mushy." If it's too thick, add a splash more water.
Flatbread preparation: Throw Self-Raising Flour and Yoghurt into a bowl. Stir until it forms a ball.
Give it a 1-minute knead on a floured surface just until smooth.
Cut into 20 small pieces. Flatten each into a thin disc with your palm or a rolling pin.
Toss them into a hot, dry non-stick pan for 1 minute per side until they puff slightly.
Serve on side with cucumber sticks.
Whisk the 12-15 eggs with the 150ml Oatly Milk. Do not add salt or pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour in the eggs.
Stir gently and constantly with a spatula. Cook until the eggs are soft and set but still moist. (Overcooking makes them rubbery and harder for toddlers to chew).
While the eggs cook, toast the 10 sliced bagels.
Place half a toasted bagel on each plate. Top with a scoop (approx. 2 tbsp) of the soft scrambled egg.
Prepare the fruit: Slice 10 apples into thin slices (peel and part boil for babies).
Place the 40g fruit portion next to the egg bagel.
Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a large pot. Add the onions, peppers, and garlic. Cook on a low heat for 15 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Stir in the rice, turmeric, and smoked paprika. Stir for 1 minute until every grain is yellow.
Stir in the 4 tbsp tomato purée. Add the 2L boiling water in three stages, stirring frequently.
When the rice is nearly tender (approx. 15 mins),
Gently stir in the 1.2kg fish cubes (1cm size) and the 300g frozen peas. Cover with a tight lid.
Cook on low for 5–8 minutes. The steam will cook the fish. Check: The fish must flake easily and reach 75°C.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest. Use a fork to lightly flake the fish through the rice, double-checking for any stray bones.
Steam the 1kg broccoli florets in a separate steamer for 6–8 minutes until very soft (fork-tender). Toss in 1 tbsp oil.
Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a large pot. Add the onions, peppers, and garlic. Cook on a low heat for 15 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Add the 1.2kg tofu cubes to the pot. Stir gently for 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the 800g rice, turmeric, and smoked paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the 4 tbsp tomato purée. Add the 2L boiling water in three stages, stirring frequently.
When the rice is nearly tender (after approx. 15 mins),
Gently stir in the 300g frozen peas. Cover with a tight lid and cook for a final 5 minutes and the rice is soft.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest.
Steam the 1kg broccoli florets in a separate steamer for 6–8 minutes until very soft (fork-tender). Toss in 1 tbsp oil.
Prep the Fruit: Place the frozen fruit in a saucepan with 100ml of the water. Simmer on low heat for 5-8 minutes until the fruit breaks down into a thick, purple/red 'jam.'
Mix: In a large bowl, combine the oats and cinnamon.

Combine: Pour the hot fruit mixture over the oats. Add the remaining 100ml-150ml of boiling water gradually, stirring until the oats are fully soaked and sticky. (If using mashed bananas, stir them in now).
Press: Line a large baking tray with greaseproof paper. Spread the mixture out and press it down firmly with the back of a spoon until it is about 2cm thick.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15 minutes until the edges are slightly golden but the middle is still soft.
Cool & Cut: Let them cool completely in the tin before slicing into 20 squares or fingers. This helps them 'set' so they don't crumble.

ingredients.name: Organic lentil rice cakes (approx. 30 cakes)
ingredients.allergens: May contain Sesame, May contain Soya

method: Cut into fingers.
1–2 Year Olds: Serve 1.5 rice cakes plus 40g fruit/veg.
3–4 Year Olds: Serve 2 rice cakes plus 40g fruit/veg.
Boil 150g lentils in 450ml water for 15–20 mins until 'mushy.' Drain any excess water and let them cool completely.
Mix the 400g cream cheese with the cold lentils and a pinch of dried parsley.
Spread the lentil-cheese mix onto 10 slices of bread. Top with the grated carrot.
Top with the remaining 10 slices. Cut each sandwich into 4 small fingers (total 40 fingers).
Prep Side Veg: Cut the 2 cucumbers into thin batons. Cut the cherry tomatoes into quarters. Give each child 2 sandwich fingers, a small pile of cucumber sticks, and 4 tomato quarters.
Mash: In a large bowl, mash the bananas into a liquid-like paste.
Mix: Whisk in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and dairy-free milk until you have a thick, smooth batter.
Cook: Heat a drop of oil in a non-stick pan. Pour small circles (8cm wide).
Flip: Cook until bubbles form on top (approx. 2 mins), flip, and cook for 1 min more.
Yield: Aim for 40–60 small pancakes (2–3 per child).
Portions — 6–12 Months: 1–2 small pancakes cut into thin, soft fingers; 80g very soft-steamed fruit.
Portions — 1–2 Years: 2 small pancakes halved for easier handling; 80g fruit.
Portions — 3–5 Years: 2–3 small pancakes; 80g fruit.
Cook 800g brown rice in plenty of unsalted water for 25–30 mins. Drain when very soft.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pot. Add onions, garlic, and ginger with 3 tbsp water. Cover and 'steam-fry' for 12–15 mins until the onions are soft.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Pour in the 400g mango purée, 800ml coconut milk, and 400ml boiling water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach the Chicken: Add the 1.5kg chicken breast cubes. Simmer on low for 12–15 mins. By using more coconut milk and less mango, check: Chicken must reach 75°C.
Cauliflower: Steam cauliflower florets separately for 6–8 mins until fork-tender. Stir them into the curry at the end.
The Finish: Stir in the lemon juice. Serve with soft brown rice & cauliflower.
Cook 800g brown rice in plenty of unsalted water for 25–30 mins. Drain when very soft.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pot. Add onions, garlic, and ginger with 3 tbsp water. Cover and 'steam-fry' for 12–15 mins until the onions are completely soft.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Pour in the 400g mango purée, 600ml coconut milk and 400ml boiling water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the rinsed chickpeas to the sauce. Simmer gently for 10–12 mins so the chickpeas soak up the mango and ginger flavors.
Steam cauliflower florets separately for 6–8 mins until fork-tender. Stir them into the curry at the end.
Stir in the lemon juice.
For younger toddlers (under 2), use a potato masher to lightly squash the chickpeas directly in the pot. This removes the 'round food' choking hazard and makes the curry easier to eat.
Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Line a baking tin.
Sift the flour and sweet cinnamon into a large bowl.
Whisk the Oatly and the oil together.
Pour the wet mix into the flour. Fold in the finely grated carrots and the raisins (including all the soaking water).
Pour into the tin. Bake for 35–45 minutes. Since there is no egg or banana, it needs the full time to set.
Cool: Let it cool completely before slicing into 20 squares.
Cut into fingers.
1–2 Year Olds: Serve 2–3 fingers (approx. 1/4 to 1/2 pitta) plus 40g fruit/veg.
3–4 Year Olds: Serve 4 fingers (a full 1/2 pitta) plus 80g fruit/veg.

ingredients.name: Mild Cheddar (use Violife cheese for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan. Sauté the diced peppers and sweetcorn for 5–8 minutes until very soft.
Add the rinsed mixed beans and the spices. Use a potato masher to coarsely smash the beans directly in the pan. (Smashing helps the beans stick to the tortilla so they don't fall out).
Place a tortilla in a dry frying pan. Spread a scoop of the bean mix over half the tortilla. Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Fold the tortilla in half to make a semi-circle. Cook for 1–2 minutes on each side until the cheese melts and the wrap is lightly golden, or place on a baking tray for 10 mins.
Slice: Cut each semi-circle into 3 small triangles (wedges).
Cut the cucumbers and carrots into thin batons (fingers).
Serve: Give each child 1 or 2 quesadilla triangles with a small pile of carrot and cucumber sticks.

ingredients.name: Organic milk or fortified plant milk

method: Peel the satsumas, remove as much of the white stringy pith as possible.
Safety cut each segment into 2-3 pieces; for younger babies you can supreme the orange (cutting the membrane out of the orange so it's soft).
Serve 1/2–1 biscuit per child depending on age.
Add milk to soften.
1–2 yrs: 1/2 Weetabix, 60–120ml milk, 1–2 segments cut into small pieces.
2–3 yrs: 1/2–1 Weetabix, 120–150ml milk, 2–3 segments cut into small pieces.
3–5 yrs: 1 Weetabix, 150ml milk, 3–4 segments cut into small pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Sauté the 4 onions with a splash of water for 10 mins until soft and sweet.
Add the beef mince. Stir and cook until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, and oregano.
Cover and simmer on low for 30–40 mins. The fresh tomatoes will melt into a sweet sauce. If it looks too thick, add a cup of water.
Boil the 800g snapped linguine in plain water until very soft. Drain and stir directly into the meat sauce.
While the pasta boils, prep the side:
Cut the 2 cucumbers into thin batons.
Cut the 300g cherry tomatoes into quarters.
Place a scoop of the beefy linguine on a plate with a small pile of the tomato and cucumber salad on the side.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Sauté the 4 onions with a splash of water for 10 mins until soft and sweet.
Add the dried red lentils, add the 1.2L of water.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, and oregano.
Cover and simmer on low for 30–40 mins. The fresh tomatoes will melt into a sweet sauce. If it looks too thick, add a cup of water.
Boil the 800g snapped linguine in plain water until very soft. Drain and stir directly into the meat sauce.
While the pasta boils, prep the side:
Cut the 2 cucumbers into thin batons.
Cut the 300g cherry tomatoes into quarters.
Place a scoop of the beefy linguine on a plate with a small pile of the tomato and cucumber salad on the side.
Place the pudding rice and 2L of the milk into a large, heavy-based pot.
Bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently so the rice doesn't stick to the bottom.
While the rice cooks, peel and finely grate the 8 apples. (Grating them helps them melt into the milk to create natural sweetness).
Stir the grated apples, the cinnamon, and the remaining milk into the pot.
Simmer for a final 10 minutes until the rice is completely soft and the apple has sweetened the pudding.
Let it stand for 10 minutes to thicken. Serve warm in small portions.

ingredients.name: large Wholemeal wraps (cut into 8 triangles each)

method: 6–12 Months: 1 triangle (20g fruit, 20g veg, soft).
1–2 Years: 1.5 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg).
3–5 Years: 2 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg).

Make the Sauce: Simmer the lentils, mushrooms, grated onion, tomatoes, water, and oregano in a pan for 15–20 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and the sauce is thick. Blend until smooth so it spreads easily and hides the lentils from picky eaters.
Assemble: Lay the pitta halves on a baking tray. Spread a generous tablespoon of the lentil-tomato sauce over each.
Cheese: Sprinkle a small amount of grated cheese on top (keep it light to manage saturated fat/salt levels).
Bake: Grill or bake at 180°C for 5–8 minutes until the cheese is melted and the pitta is warm but still soft (do not overcook, as hard pitta is a choking risk for infants).
Toast bread until golden.
Spread with cream cheese.
Cut into squares/triangles and serve.
Serve with 1 selection of fruit.
Serve a cup of 100ml of milk.

ingredients.name: Mild White Cheddar (Violife cheese for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Scrub 10 baking potatoes, prick with a fork, bake at 200°C for 1 hour until the centers are very soft.
In a large pot, sauté 4 minced garlic cloves in 2 tbsp oil for 1 minute. Stir in the smoked paprika, passata, and 200ml water. Simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Stir in 4 cans of rinsed cannellini beans. Simmer for 10 more minutes until the beans are soft and the sauce is thick.
Boil or steam 600g frozen sweetcorn for 5 minutes.
Halve the potatoes. Top each half with a scoop of beans and 20g grated cheese. Serve sweetcorn on the side.
Scrub the outside of all melons thoroughly before cutting to remove any soil bacteria. Remove the rinds and all seeds.
Safety First: Avoid using a melon baller for children under 5. The round spheres are a significant choking risk as they are firm and slippery.
6–9 Months: Slice the melons into long, flat rectangular fingers (about the size of two adult fingers) so babies can grip the fruit and gum the end.
9–12 Months: Once the pincer grip develops, cut the fruit into flat, bite-sized pieces or small sticks roughly the size of a thumb.
1–5 Years: Serve as small, thin chunks or wedges. Ensure pieces are not so large that a child might attempt to swallow them whole.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan. Add the diced onion and garlic with 3 tbsp of water. Cover with a lid and cook on low for 10 minutes until very soft. Let cool.
Grate the 400g courgette. Wrap in a clean tea towel and squeeze as hard as possible to remove all liquid.
In a large bowl, stir the flour and herbs.
Stir in the squeezed courgette and the softened onion/garlic mix.
Gradually pour in the 650ml Oatly. Stir until it forms a thick, sticky dough. (If it feels too dry, add a tiny splash more Oatly).
Press the dough into a lined baking tray (about 2cm thick). Score the top into 20-30 finger shapes with a knife.
Bake at 180°C (Fan) for 25–30 minutes until golden and firm.
Let it cool completely before cutting into fingers.
Portions — 6–12 Months: 1–2 fingers (20g fruit, 20g veg, soft). 1–2 Years: 2–3 fingers (40g fruit, 40g veg). 3–5 Years: 3–4 fingers (40g fruit, 40g veg).
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add onions, garlic, and carrots with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 mins until soft.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the 1.5kg chicken cubes. Stir for 5 mins.
Add the chopped apricots, diced courgettes, and 500ml of the boiling water. Cover and simmer for 15 mins until the chicken is tender (75°C).
Stir in the 300g frozen peas and cook for 2 more minutes.
In a separate large bowl, put the 800g dry couscous. Pour over the remaining 1L boiling water. Cover with a lid or plate and let it sit for 5 minutes until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Gently fold the chicken and vegetable mixture (and all its sweet juices) into the fluffed couscous.

ingredients.name: Chicken (printed as-is on source card; likely should read Black Eyed Beans — see _note)

method: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add onions, garlic, and diced carrots with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 12 mins until the carrots are soft.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, and turmeric for 1 minute to release the flavor.
Add the rinsed black-eyed beans, chopped apricots, diced courgettes, and 500ml of the boiling water.
Cover and simmer on low for 15 mins. The beans will soak up the spices and the apricots will soften into the sauce.
Stir in the 300g frozen peas and cook for 2 more minutes.
In a separate large bowl, put the 800g dry couscous. Pour over the remaining 1L boiling water. Cover and let sit for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Fold the bean and vegetable mixture into the fluffed couscous. Stir well so the couscous absorbs all the sweet Moroccan juices.
Prepare the apples: peel and core them. Steam or boil in a small amount of water for 5–8 minutes until very soft. Mash thoroughly.
Cook the Oats: In a large pot, combine the oats, milk, water, and cinnamon.
Simmer: Bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 5–10 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until creamy and the oats are soft.
Combine: Stir the mashed apple directly into the porridge. If it's too thick, add a splash more milk or water.
Cool: Let the porridge sit for a few minutes before serving. It should be warm, not hot, for young children.
Grate the 2 courgettes. Place them in a clean tea towel and squeeze out all the water. This is vital so the meatballs don't fall apart.
In a large bowl, mix the turkey mince, squeezed courgette, grated onion, minced garlic, and dried herbs.
Roll the mixture into 40–60 small 'Micky Me-Size' balls (about the size of a large marble).
Lightly oil two baking trays. Place the meatballs on the trays and bake at 180°C (Fan) for 15–18 minutes until cooked through (75°C).
Place 600g bulgur wheat in a bowl. Pour over 1.2L boiling water. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes until soft. Fluff with a fork.
Finely dice the 2 cucumbers.
Quarter the 400g cherry tomatoes (essential for safety).
Serve: Give each child 2 or 3 meatballs on a bed of the bulgur with a side of cucumber salad.
Place the rinsed butter beans in a large bowl. Use a potato masher or fork to mash them into a thick paste. (Leave some texture for older children).
Stir in the squeezed courgette, grated onion, minced garlic, oats, and dried herbs. The oats will soak up the moisture and make the mixture firm enough to roll.
Roll the mixture into 40–60 small balls.
Lightly oil two baking trays. Place the balls on the trays and brush the tops with a little oil. Bake at 190°C (Fan) for 20–25 minutes until golden and firm.
Place 600g bulgur wheat in a bowl. Pour over 1.2L boiling water. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes until soft. Fluff with a fork.
Serve: Give each child 2 or 3 bean balls on a bed of the bulgur with cucumber salad.

ingredients.name: Organic Greek style Yoghurt (Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for Vegan/Dairy-free)

method: Core the pears. Peel them for children under 1 to remove the choking risk. Slice each pear into 8 even wedges.
Place wedges in a baking dish. Pour over the 4 tbsp water and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Cover the dish tightly with foil to trap the steam.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15–20 minutes until 'fork-tender' (they should squash easily between your fingers).
Let them cool. Serve the soft wedges with a dollop of plain yoghurt for dipping.

ingredients.name: Veg (cherry tomatoes quartered, carrots — soft for babies)

method: Cut into fingers.
Under 1s: 1 oatcake plus 20g fruit and 20g veg.
3–4 Year Olds: 1.5–2 oatcakes plus 40g fruit and 40g veg.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek style Yoghurt (Oatly Greek style oatgurt for dairy-free)

method: Cook the pasta in plenty of unsalted boiling water until soft. Important: Drain the pasta and rinse it immediately under cold water to stop the cooking and cool it down.
Boil or steam the sweetcorn for 5 minutes until tender. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Finely dice the cucumber.
In a very large bowl, stir together the yoghurt, the dried herbs, and the flaked tuna.
Add the cold pasta, cold sweetcorn, and diced cucumber to the yoghurt mixture.
Fold everything together until every piece of pasta is coated in the creamy tuna dressing.
Keep in the fridge until ready to serve.
Cook the pasta in plenty of unsalted boiling water until very soft. Drain and rinse under cold water until completely cooled.
Boil or steam the sweetcorn for 5 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Pat the tofu dry with a clean cloth. Use your fingers to crumble it into small chunks (about the size of a pea) into a large bowl.
Stir the turmeric and dried parsley into the crumbled tofu until it is evenly coated and yellow.
Add the Oatly oatgurt to the tofu and stir until creamy.
Fold in the cold pasta, cold sweetcorn, and diced cucumber.
Keep in the fridge until ready to serve.

ingredients.name: Organic whole/semi milk (use Oatly for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Serve 1/2-1 biscuit per child depending on age.
Add warm milk to soften.
Add banana slices.
Portions: 1-2yrs: 1/2 Weetabix, 60-120ml milk, 1-2 tbsp banana; 2-3yrs: 1/2-1 Weetabix, 120-150ml milk, 2-3 tbsp banana; 3-5yrs: 1 Weetabix, 150ml milk, 3-4 tbsp banana.
Steam the cauliflower florets for 8-10 minutes until very soft. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add the ginger, garlic, peppers, and grated carrots with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 mins until soft.
Stir in the coriander and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed chickpeas, 400ml coconut milk, and 600ml Oatly.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Use a potato masher to lightly squash some of the chickpeas directly in the pot (this makes the sauce thick and removes the 'round food' choking hazard).
Boil the snapped noodles in plain water until very soft. Drain and stir them directly into the chickpea curry.
Scoop the creamy noodles into 20 bowls.
Place the soft cauliflower florets on the side.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-Style Yoghurt (1.5-2kg) (use Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Defrost strawberry fruits as per manufacturer's instructions.
Mash the fruit a little, add to yoghurt and stir.
Cover with cling film and refrigerate at 8C or below until serving.

ingredients.name: [ingredient name missing in source - printed only as '400g']

method: In a large bowl, stir together the 800g flour and 2 tsp herbs.
In a separate jug, mix the 300ml passata, 300ml Oatly, and 2 tbsp oil.
Pour the wet mixture into the flour. Stir with a wooden spoon until it forms a thick, soft dough. (If it feels too dry to stick together, add a tiny splash more Oatly).
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead gently for just 1 minute until smooth.
Press the dough into a lined baking tray so it is about 2cm thick. Use a knife to score the top into 20-30 finger shapes.
Bake at 180C (Fan) for 20-25 minutes until firm and lightly golden on the edges.
Cool: Let it cool completely in the tray, then snap into fingers.
Serve with cucumber & carrot fingers (make sure cucumber is peeled and carrots are part boiled and in fingers).
Portions: 6-12 months: 1-2 fingers (20g fruit, 20g veg, soft); 1-2 years: 2-3 fingers (40g fruit, 40g veg); 3-5 years: 3-4 fingers (40g fruit, 40g veg).
Grate the courgettes and carrots. Place them in a clean tea towel and squeeze as hard as you can to remove the green/orange water.
In a large bowl, stir together the 800g flour, dried herbs, and 200g sweetcorn.
Add the flaked tuna (or crumbled tofu for vegans) and the squeezed grated veg to the flour.
Gradually pour in the 750ml Oatly. Stir gently until it forms a thick, wet dough. (Do not over-mix or they will be heavy).
Use the 1 tbsp oil to lightly grease 20 muffin tins (or use paper cases). Spoon the mixture in.
Cook at 180C (Fan) for 25-30 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Let them cool completely. They will firm up as they cool, making them perfect for a light tea.
Serve with a side of cucumber & peppers.
Boil the 150g lentils in 450ml water for 15 minutes until 'mushy' and the water is absorbed. Let them cool completely.
Grate the courgettes and carrots. Squeeze them very hard in a clean tea towel to remove all excess water.
In a large bowl, stir the 800g flour, herbs, and sweetcorn.
Add the cold mashed lentils and the squeezed grated veg to the flour.
Gradually pour in the 750ml Oatly. Stir gently until it forms a thick, wet dough.
Use the 1 tbsp oil to grease 20 muffin tins or use paper cases. Spoon the mixture in.
Bake at 180C (Fan) for 25-30 minutes until golden and firm.
Let them cool completely. They will firm up as they sit, making them easy for toddlers to hold.
Prepare the apples: peel and core them. Steam or boil in a small amount of water for 5-8 minutes until very soft. Mash thoroughly.
Cook the oats: in a large pot, combine the oats, milk, water, and cinnamon.
Simmer: bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until creamy and the oats are soft.
Combine: stir the mashed apple directly into the porridge. If it's too thick, add a splash more milk or water.
Cool: let the porridge sit for a few minutes before serving. It should be warm, not hot, for young children.
The mash: boil the 2.5kg potatoes in plain water for 20 mins until very soft. Drain well.
Make it Mediterranean: mash the potatoes with the 500ml Oatly, 4 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tsp of the dried oregano until completely smooth and creamy. Keep warm.
The tomato sauce: in a bowl, mix the 1kg passata, diced red peppers, minced garlic, and the remaining 1 tsp oregano.
Bake the fish: grease a large deep baking tray with 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Pour half of the tomato sauce into the bottom. Lay the 20 cod pieces on top, then pour the rest of the sauce over the fish.
Cook: cover the tray with foil to keep the fish moist. Bake at 180C (Fan) for 15-18 minutes until the cod flakes easily with a fork.
The veg: while the fish bakes, boil or steam the 800g green beans for 5-7 mins until tender.
Assemble: place a scoop of the Herby Oatly Mash on a plate. Top with a piece of Baked Cod and a spoonful of the Tomato & Pepper Sauce. Serve the green beans on the side.
Boil the 2.5kg potatoes in plain water for 20 mins until very soft. Drain well.
Mash the potatoes with the 500ml Oatly, 4 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tsp of the dried oregano until completely smooth. Keep warm.
In a large bowl, mix the 1kg passata, diced red peppers, minced garlic, and the remaining 1 tsp oregano.
Grease a large deep baking tray with 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Pour half of the tomato sauce into the bottom. Lay the 20 tofu cubes on top, then pour the rest of the sauce over the tofu.
Cover the tray with foil (to keep the tofu tender). Bake at 180C (Fan) for 20 minutes until the sauce is bubbly and the tofu is hot throughout.
While the tofu bakes, boil or steam the 800g green beans for 5-7 mins until tender.
Place a scoop of the Herby Oatly Mash on a plate. Top with the Baked Tofu and a spoonful of the Tomato & Pepper Sauce. Serve the green beans on the side.
Scrub the outside of all melons thoroughly before cutting to remove any soil bacteria. Remove the rinds and all seeds.
Safety first: avoid using a melon baller for children under 5. The round spheres are a significant choking risk as they are firm and slippery.

Cut for age groups: 6-9 months - slice into long, flat rectangular fingers (about the size of two adult fingers) so babies can grip and gum the end; 9-12 months - once the pincer grip develops, cut into flat, bite-sized pieces or small sticks the size of a thumb; 1-5 years - serve as small, thin chunks or wedges, ensuring pieces are not so large a child might swallow them whole.
Serving guide - 6-9 months (early weaning): mashed or long flat rectangular fingers, portion 2-3 thin fingers for self-feeding.
Serving guide - 9-12 months (pincer grasp): small flat bite-sized chunks or thin thumb-sized sticks, portion a small handful of pieces.
Serving guide - 1-5 years (pre-school): mixed medley of thin chunks or small wedges, portion 1 small bowl (approx. 40-50g).

ingredients.name: Organic lentil rice cakes (approx. 30 cakes)
ingredients.allergens: May contain Sesame, May contain Soya

method: Cut into fingers.
1-2 Year Olds: serve 1.5 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg.
3-4 Year Olds: serve 2 rice cakes, 40g fruit/veg.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a very large pot. Add the onions, ginger, and garlic with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 mins until very soft.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the grated carrots, tomato puree, and the 1.5kg chicken cubes. Stir for 2 mins.
Add the 800g rinsed rice and the 400g frozen peas. Stir well.
Pour in the 600ml coconut milk and 1.2L boiling water. Stir once, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Put a tight-fitting lid on the pot. Turn the heat to very low and cook for 15-20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the pot sit, covered, for another 5 minutes.
Finish: fluff the biriyani with a fork. The grated carrots will have 'melted' into the rice, making it naturally sweet. Check: chicken must hit 75C.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a very large pot. Add the onions, ginger, and garlic with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 mins until very soft.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, and turmeric for 1 minute to release the aroma.
Add the grated carrots, tomato puree, and the rinsed chickpeas. Stir for 2 mins to coat everything in the spices.
Add the 800g rinsed rice and the 400g frozen peas. Stir well.
Pour in the 600ml coconut milk and 1.2L boiling water. Stir once, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Put a tight-fitting lid on the pot. Turn the heat to very low and cook for 15-20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the pot sit, covered, for another 5 minutes. This ensures the rice is fully cooked.
For younger toddlers (under 2), use a potato masher to lightly squash some of the chickpeas directly in the pot to remove any round-food choking hazards.

ingredients.name: Organic large eggs (15-20; use Avocado for vegan)
Organic whole milk (use Oatly for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Add the Oatly and whisk until well combined and frothy.
Add the oil to a large non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture. Let it sit for 20 seconds, then gently stir with a spatula. Keep moving the eggs slowly until they are soft and creamy. Do not overcook, as they will become rubbery.
While the eggs are cooking, toast the wholewheat bread.
Spread the eggs evenly over the toast with spread. For toddlers, it is best to cut the toast into 'soldiers' (strips) to make it easier for them to pick up.
Serve with 1 selection of fruit. Make sure these are soft fingers for babies so part boil.
Saute: soften the onions, grated carrots, grated courgettes in a splash of water for 10-12 minutes.
Brown: add the turkey mince to the pan. Cook until browned, breaking up any large lumps. Stir in the garlic and tomato puree for 1 minute.
Simmer: pour in the tinned tomatoes and herbs. Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes. The grated carrots will melt into the sauce, naturally thickening and sweetening it.
Pasta: cook the wholewheat spaghetti in boiling water for 10-12 minutes until tender. Drain, then toss with the sauce.
Serve with side salad.
Saute: soften the onions, grated carrots, grated courgettes in a splash of water for 10-12 minutes.
Brown: add the butterbeans. Stir in the garlic and tomato puree for 1 minute.
Simmer: pour in the tinned tomatoes and herbs. Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes. The grated carrots will melt into the sauce, naturally thickening and sweetening it.
Pasta: cook the wholewheat spaghetti in boiling water for 10-12 minutes until tender. Drain, then toss with the sauce.
Serve with side salad.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-Style Yoghurt (1.5-2kg) (use Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy-free)
Satsumas/clementines (easy to peel, usually seedless) or Oranges (10-12)

method: Peel the oranges or satsumas. Remove as much of the white stringy pith as possible.
Cut each segment into 2 or 3 bite-sized pieces. For younger toddlers, you can 'supreme' the oranges (removing the skin/membrane) so they are extra soft, but small chopped segments are usually fine.
Place a generous dollop of yoghurt into 20 small bowls or ramekins.
Divide the orange pieces evenly across the bowls, sitting them on top of the yoghurt.
Sprinkle with a tiny bit of sweet cinnamon if you like. Serve chilled.
Spread vitalite on the oatcakes and serve with fruit & veg.
Under 1s: 1 oatcake, 20g fruit, 20g veg.
3-4 Year Olds: 1.5-2 oatcakes, 40g fruit, 40g veg.

ingredients.name: Mild White Cheddar (use Violife cheese for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Toss the potato wedges with 2 tbsp oil on a large baking tray. Bake at 200C (180C fan) for 30-35 minutes until the insides are fluffy and soft. (Do not let the skins get too hard or crunchy for toddlers.)
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add the minced garlic and cook on low for 1 minute (don't brown).
Stir in the smoked paprika and 1.2kg passata. Simmer on low for 15 mins to naturally sweeten the tomatoes.
Add the rinsed cannellini beans. Simmer for another 10 mins until thick and soft.
Boil or steam the 600g sweetcorn for 5 minutes. Drain well.
Place 4 or 5 wedges in each bowl. Top with a generous scoop of the garlic beans, a spoonful of sweetcorn, and a sprinkle of grated cheese.
Serve with the cucumber batons on the side of the plate.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek-style Yoghurt (1.5-2kg) (use Plain Oatly Greek style oatgurt for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Place the dry oats and sweet cinnamon in a large pan over a medium heat. Stir for 2-3 minutes until they smell slightly toasty.
Turn off the heat. Pour the 150ml of boiling water over the toasted oats and stir well.
Cover the pan and let the oats sit for 10 minutes. They will soak up the water and become soft and 'chewy' rather than hard and crunchy, making them safe for small children.
While the oats rest, peel the kiwis and dice them into small, 1cm cubes.
Place a generous dollop of Greek yoghurt into 20 small bowls.
Top each bowl with a spoonful of the softened cinnamon oats and the diced kiwi.
Stir slightly before giving to the children so the yoghurt coats the oats.
Boil 800g rice in a large pot of plain water until very soft. Drain and keep warm.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add the minced garlic, diced peppers, and grated courgettes with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the 1.2kg beef mince. Cook until browned, breaking it up thoroughly with a wooden spoon.
Stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, tomato puree, passata, mixed beans, and sweetcorn & peas.
Simmer on low for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and the beef is tender.
While the beef simmers, steam or boil the broccoli florets in plain water for 6-8 minutes until 'fork-tender' (very soft). Drain well.
Place a scoop of rice and the beef mix [source text says 'Mexican beef mix' - see recipe note] in a bowl. Serve the soft broccoli florets on the side.

ingredients.name: Organic black beans (unit not specified in source, likely tins)

method: Boil 800g rice in a large pot of plain water until very soft. Drain and keep warm.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot. Add the minced garlic, diced peppers, and grated courgettes with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the black beans.
Stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, tomato puree, passata, mixed beans, and sweetcorn & peas.
Simmer on low for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick [source text says 'and the beef is tender' - see recipe note, this dish has no beef].
While simmering, steam or boil the broccoli florets in plain water for 6-8 minutes until 'fork-tender' (very soft). Drain well.
Place a scoop of rice and the black bean mix [source text says 'Mexican black bean mix' - see recipe note] in a bowl. Serve the soft broccoli florets on the side.
Preheat oven to 180C (160C fan). Line a muffin tin with 20 mini-muffin cases or grease a tin well.
Sift the wholemeal flour, bicarb, and baking powder into a bowl (tip any bran left in the sieve back into the bowl).
In a separate bowl, whisk the mashed bananas and Oatly together until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir gently until just combined - do not over-mix or the muffins will be heavy.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Spoon into cases. Bake for 15-20 minutes (mini muffins) or 20-25 minutes (larger ones) until they spring back when touched.
Let them cool completely. Wholemeal, oil-free bakes can be a bit sticky when hot, so they are best served once cooled.

ingredients.name: Large Wholemeal wraps (3-4; cut into 8 triangles each = 24-32 pieces)
Fruit (choose from plums, peaches, grapes quartered)

method: 6-12 Months: 1 triangle (20g fruit, 20g veg, soft).
1-2 Years: 1.5 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg).
3-5 Years: 2 triangles (40g fruit, 40g veg).

ingredients.name: Organic Feta Cheese (use Violife soft feta for vegan/dairy-free)

method: Cook the 800g orzo in plenty of plain boiling water for 8-10 minutes until very soft. Drain and rinse under cold water immediately to stop it from clumping.
Quarter the 400g cherry tomatoes lengthways (essential for safety).
Finely slice the spring onions.
Dice the 3 red peppers into tiny 5mm-1cm cubes to match the size of the orzo.
The dressing: in a very large bowl, whisk the 1 tbsp olive oil, 100ml Oatly, and 2 tbsp dried oregano.
Combine: add the cold orzo, rinsed cannellini beans, sweetcorn, diced peppers, and sliced spring onions to the bowl.
The tomatoes: add the quartered cherry tomatoes. Stir well so the juices mix with the Oatly to coat the small orzo grains.
The feta: gently fold in the 400g crumbled feta. The feta will naturally 'cream' into the orzo as it sits.
Chill: keep in the fridge until the tea service. Give it a good stir before serving to loosen the grains.

ingredients.name: Cream Cheese (quantity not specified in printed Ingredients list - Portions section calls for 15-30g per child; see recipe note)

method: Peel, core, and slice the pears into soft, thin segments. If they are very firm, steam them for 2 minutes so they are easy for toddlers to chew.
Lightly toast the wholemeal bagel halves.
Spread a generous layer of avocado.
Cut each bagel half into 4 smaller segments (triangles) or 'soldiers' to make them safer and easier for small hands to hold.
Serve with the sliced pears.

Portions: 1-2 years: 1/2 bagel with 1 heaped tsp (15g) cream cheese and 2-3 soft pear slices; 2-3 years: 1/2 bagel with 2 tsp (20g) cream cheese and 3-4 soft pear slices; 3-5 years: 1 bagel with 1 tbsp (30g) cream cheese and 4-5 soft pear slices.
Boil the 2kg potatoes and 6 sliced carrots in plain water for 15-20 minutes until very soft.
Drain the vegetables but save 1.2L of the cooking water in a jug. This 'pot liquor' contains all the natural vitamins and flavor for your gravy.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pan. Add the minced garlic and 1.5kg chicken cubes. Saute for 8-10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (75C).
Add the 800g green beans and 400g peas to the chicken pan for the last 5-7 minutes to steam through until tender.

Make the veg gravy: whisk the 4 tbsp tomato puree and 2 tsp thyme into the 1.2L saved vegetable water. Take one large scoop (approx. 100g) of the boiled carrots and potatoes and add them to the liquid. Use a stick blender to whizz until completely smooth. The starch from the potato and sweetness from the carrot makes a thick, savoury gravy.
Place the boiled potatoes and carrots on the plate. Top with the chicken, green beans, and peas. Pour over a generous scoop of the veg gravy.
Cook the lentils: boil 400g red lentils in 1L water for 15-20 mins until 'mushy' and water is absorbed. Let them cool slightly.
Make the loaf: in a large bowl, mix the cooked lentils, 200g oats, 400ml Oatly, squeezed courgette, 2 cloves minced garlic, and 1 tsp thyme.
Press the mixture into two greased loaf tins (approx. 2-3cm thick). Bake at 190C (Fan) for 25-30 minutes until firm. Let it sit for 10 mins before slicing into 20 fingers.
Boil the sides: boil the 2kg new potatoes and 6 sliced carrots in plain water for 15 mins until very soft.
Save the water: drain the veg but save 1L of the cooking water for your gravy.
Summer veg: boil the 600g green beans and 400g peas for 3-5 mins. Drain.
Serve: place a slice of lentil loaf on the plate with the potatoes, carrots, sweetcorn, and peas. Pour the veg gravy over the loaf (see main dish for gravy recipe).
Place the pudding rice (method states 400g, ingredients list states 250g - see recipe note) and 2L of the milk into a large, heavy-based pot.
Bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to low. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently so the rice doesn't stick to the bottom.
While the rice cooks, peel and finely grate the 8 apples. (Grating them helps them melt into the milk to create natural sweetness).
Stir the grated apples, the 2 tsp cinnamon, and the remaining 200ml of milk into the pot.
Simmer for a final 10 minutes until the rice is completely soft and the apple has sweetened the pudding.
Let it stand for 10 minutes to thicken. Serve warm in small bowls.
Cut into fingers (soft fruit fingers or part boiled for babies).
1-2 Year Olds: serve 2-3 fingers (approx. 1/4 to 1/2 pitta), 40g fruit/veg.
3-4 Year Olds: serve 4 fingers (a full 1/2 pitta), 80g fruit/veg.

ingredients.name: Organic Plain Greek style Yoghurt (use Oatly Greek style oatgurt for dairy-free)

method: Place 12 eggs in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Drain and sit in cold water before peeling.
In a large bowl, mash the hard-boiled eggs with a fork until very fine. Stir in the 200g yoghurt, 1 tsp chives, and the sniped cress. Mix until creamy.
Spread the egg mix thickly onto 10 slices of bread. Top with the remaining 10 slices.
Remove crusts if necessary for 1-year-olds. Cut each sandwich into 4 small triangles or fingers (making 40 pieces total).
Wash the 400g cherry tomatoes. Important: cut every tomato into quarters (lengthways) to prevent choking.
Place 2 sandwich fingers on a plate with 4-6 tomato quarters on the side.
Place the rinsed chickpeas in a large bowl. Add the 200ml Oatly (or yoghurt) and dried herbs.
Use a potato masher or a stick blender to whizz the chickpeas until they are a completely smooth paste. (This removes the 'round-food' choking hazard).
Stir in the sniped cress by hand so it is evenly mixed through the chickpea paste.
Spread the chickpea mix thickly onto 10 slices of bread. Top with the remaining 10 slices.
Remove the crusts if needed. Cut each sandwich into 4 small fingers or triangles.
Wash the 400g cherry tomatoes. Important: cut every single tomato into quarters lengthways to ensure they are safe.
Place 2-3 sandwich fingers on a plate with the tomato quarters on the side.
